s1.syndrome_frame: A firm, fixed mass in the breast with a history of prior breast cancer treatment
salient_findings: 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space on mammography
Lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography
key_facts: 59-year-old woman
Lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
History of breast-conserving surgery
Endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast
Prior carcinoma in the upper inner quadrant of the left breast
Six years since prior breast cancer treatment
Mass is fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Overlying skin is uninvolved
No palpable axillary lymph nodes
Lesion increased in size on three-month follow-up

shortlist.label: Locoregional breast cancer recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: History of prior breast cancer and a new, growing mass in the same breast

shortlist.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of radiation therapy to the breast and a new, firm mass

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Sarcoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, fixed mass in the breast with a history of prior breast cancer treatment

shortlist.label: Fat necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast-conserving surgery and radiation, with a new mass in the breast

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of breast-conserving surgery and radiation to the left breast, and now presents with a new lump in a different quadrant of the same breast, which has increased in size on follow-up, suggesting a recurrence of the original breast cancer.

rejected.label: Radiation-induced sarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, the time frame of six years since radiation therapy is relatively short for the development of a radiation-induced sarcoma, which typically occurs after a longer latency period.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: The description of the mass as fixed to the pectoralis major muscle and having increased in size does not specifically suggest a Phyllodes tumor, which is typically characterized by its rapid growth and large size at presentation.

rejected.label: Sarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Sarcomas of the breast are rare and the clinical presentation in this case, with a history of breast cancer and radiation, is more suggestive of a recurrence of the original breast cancer than a primary sarcoma.

rejected.label: Fat necrosis
rejected.why: The clinical and imaging findings, including the mass being fixed to the pectoralis major muscle and increasing in size, are not typical of fat necrosis, which usually presents as a palpable mass or mammographic abnormality that is often related to trauma or surgery.
